key_insight: AgentAM gives engineers natural-language access to LPBF surrogate models, enabling low-spatter process optimization with explicit margins from geometry-derived defect boundaries.
engineering_relevance: For SS316L, the system could reduce programming barriers to process-window exploration while helping engineers avoid fragile settings near defect thresholds.
method: Connect an LLM agent to CFD-trained polynomial surrogates through the Model Context Protocol.
Predict melt pool geometry and spatter, then classify geometry-derived defect regimes.
Scan power–velocity windows and optimize spatter subject to constraints and defect-boundary margins.
evidence_signal: Trained on 279 single-track simulations, the surrogates achieved melt pool R² ≥ 0.95 and test spatter R² = 0.83; across 725 agent benchmark runs, all 65 feasible optimization runs met stated constraints, with a median 1.0% gap to the brute-force optimum.
watch_item: Results are simulation-based and limited to the trained SS316L range; robustness estimates depend on assumed process drift and sampled model residuals, not shop-floor validation.
paper_title: AgentAM: An AI Agent for Spatter- and Defect-Aware Process Optimization in Laser Powder Bed Fusion
